round1.about: The blind ladder's answers (docs/moth-10): fresh reviewers, the sheets' crops shuffled under A to E; wear_check.py reads 'reviewers' (the latest round) against blind/key.json. material_ok is mine, from what each reviewer said the sheet showed before reading the descriptions: false only if they named a different material.

material_seen.alloy: satin silver anodised aluminium fittings and tubes on a white deck; reads as real alloy except E, where the oxide looks like glittery granite
material_seen.carbon: glossy dark gunmetal carbon tubes with a faint twill; reads as carbon or painted metal tube, and the aged amber ones read like brown plastic
material_seen.grip: matt black ribbed rubber grip on a tube; reads as rubber, but D looks like grey concrete or plaster
material_seen.mesh: dark smooth trampoline sheet with laced edge; reads like a vinyl tarp, not an open woven mesh (no strands or gaps visible)
material_seen.paint: glossy white painted hull topside and bottom; reads as white gelcoat or paint, but A and B look like a lichen-patterned stone texture
material_seen.paint.foil: satin dark grey painted foil and strut; reads as painted foil, except A, which looks like rusty steel
material_seen.rope: thin orange control lines over a white deck and dark mesh; reads as plain cord or wire at this scale, braid not resolvable
material_seen.sail: clear laminate sail film with a fine scrim grid; reads as clear film when new, and like yellow crumpled cellophane or parchment when aged

least_real.alloy: In E the white oxide is a high-contrast black-and-white glitter speckle covering every surface (tubes, base plate, track) like granite, instead of white powder gathered in crevices and round screws.
least_real.carbon: B's chalked coat is a uniform grey-white camouflage blotching (even on the moulded clamp block), and the amber of A and D tints the tubes a pinkish brown like plastic, not yellowed clear coat over a visible weave.
least_real.grip: D's chalky grip is a flat light grey with uniform fine speckle, reading as concrete or plaster, and the cracks are not visible.
least_real.mesh: At every level the mesh is a smooth, blurry, opaque sheet with no visible strands or light through gaps, and E's mildew is an even leopard-spot speckle over the whole surface like terrazzo rather than patches.
least_real.paint: The chalking in A and B is a mottled grey-green lichen pattern tiled evenly across the whole topside, with ruler-straight full-height dark stripes, rather than chalky fade with streaks that start at fittings.
least_real.paint.foil: A's foil is turned an orange-brown rust colour all over, like corroded steel, instead of chalky grey paint chipped to white filler and grey primer.
least_real.rope: The lines are too thin and smooth to show braid or fuzz, so their age shows only as a colour shift, and in C they turn a flat grey that is barely visible against the dirty mesh.
least_real.sail: The white creases are random worm-like squiggles, like veins or marbling, rather than straight or angular fold lines, and C's mildew is large soft dark blotches rather than fine specks.

material_seen.alloy: silver anodised alloy fittings and stanchion base on a white deck, with carbon tubes and a clear sail; it reads as real alloy up to the most worn crop, where the fittings turn into grey-white speckled granite or glitter
material_seen.carbon: dark glossy carbon tubes (wing frame and gantry) going brown or tan with age; real carbon when new, but the aged ones look like brown-painted or wooden poles, and the worst fitting looks like a lump of grey stone
material_seen.grip: black ribbed rubber twist grip on a tube; convincing as rubber, and the oldest version reads as dusty grey plastic
material_seen.mesh: dark woven trampoline mesh laced to a frame; at this distance it reads as smooth blotchy grey fabric or vinyl, not an open weave, and the oldest is a speckled tan fabric like camouflage
material_seen.paint: white painted hull side and transom with alloy fittings; the new and polished crops read as real gloss paint, while the aged ones read as grey marble or wallpaper-like vertical streaks and the most worn fittings as granite
material_seen.paint.foil: satin dark grey painted foil strut and wing; real paint when new, and the most worn one looks like rusty brown steel more than chalky paint
material_seen.rope: orange braided control lines and grey shrouds over a white deck, mesh and sail; convincing when new, while the old lines turn a flat grey-green and the mesh turns a sandy speckled carpet
material_seen.sail: clear laminate sail with a scrim grid, going yellow and milky; reads as clear film when new, and the aged crops look like beige paper with white squiggles (like veined marble) more than creased film

least_real.alloy: In E the white aluminium oxide is a coarse, even salt-and-pepper speckle over whole fittings and the track, so they look like granite or glitter rather than crusty oxide in the crevices and round the screws.
least_real.carbon: In B the chalked, flaking coat is the same granite-like speckle over the alloy fitting and a flat tan wash over the tubes, so the carbon reads as painted wood or stone with no weave showing through.
least_real.grip: In D the grime and cracking are a uniform pale dusty tint that also turns the lacing and sail beige, so the grip looks dusted with flour rather than grime packed into the ribs and cracks in the rubber.
least_real.mesh: The mesh never shows open gaps or a woven strand texture, and in E the mildew is an even all-over speckle on a tan sheet, like camouflage cloth rather than patchy black mildew on PVC strands.
least_real.paint: In A and B the black streaks are dense, evenly spaced vertical stripes over a grey marble-like mottle across the whole topside, not runs starting at the fittings, so it reads as a texture tile rather than weathered paint.
least_real.paint.foil: A's strut and foil are an orange-brown rust colour, which painted composite foils never take on, so they look like corroded steel rather than chalked grey paint chipped to filler and primer.
least_real.rope: In C the lines lose their orange entirely and go a flat dark grey-green, and the mesh under them becomes a uniform speckled sand carpet, so the aging looks like a colour filter on the whole scene rather than worn braid.
least_real.sail: In A to C the white creases are thin, random, curly squiggles evenly scattered like marble veins, where real laminate creases are straighter crease lines concentrated near the battens and the luff.

material_seen.alloy: satin silver metal fittings on a white hull; reads as anodised alloy when new, but the most worn ones look like speckled granite, not metal
material_seen.carbon: dark grey to brown satin tubes; read as painted or plastic tubes more than carbon twill (the weave barely shows)
material_seen.grip: ribbed matt black rubber grip on a tube; reads as real rubber
material_seen.mesh: black to grey-brown trampoline fabric; reads as a solid tarp or felt sheet, not an open mesh you can see through
material_seen.paint: white painted hull side; reads as gloss paint when new, as streaked plaster or marble when old
material_seen.paint.foil: satin grey painted foil and strut; reads as paint, except one crop that looks like rusty steel
material_seen.rope: thin orange control lines and dark shrouds over a white deck; too thin to show a braid, they read as coloured wire
material_seen.sail: translucent film sail with a diamond scrim; reads as laminate when new, as veined marble or paper when old

least_real.alloy: In E the white oxide covers every fitting as an even black-and-white glitter, like granite or terrazzo, when it should only collect in crevices and round the screws.
least_real.carbon: In B the tubes go a flat brownish grey, like wood, with no chalky flaking and no fuzzy weave showing, and the end fitting has the same granite speckle.
least_real.grip: In D the chalky grip is a flat, even grey like felt or concrete, with no visible cracks, and the grime is not picked out in the ribs.
least_real.mesh: None of the crops shows gaps in the weave, so the mesh reads as a solid tarp, and E's mildew is a uniform printed speckle over the whole panel instead of patches.
least_real.paint: In B the black streaks are evenly spaced vertical smears across the whole topside, not runs from the fittings, and the fittings above have turned to speckled granite.
least_real.paint.foil: In A the grey foil has gone a rusty orange-brown, which looks like corroded steel rather than faded or polished paint.
least_real.rope: In C the lines just fade into thin uniform grey threads with no visible fuzz or stiffness, and the eye goes to the mildew-speckled mesh instead.
least_real.sail: In C the white creases are wormy, branching squiggles like marble veins rather than straight fold lines in film, laid over a uniformly mottled yellow.
